- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% prior) to reduce overfitting.
